lines.note: 1 page, 7 fields, 1 file upload required only for one leave type, 1 calculated field (working days), save as draft. The two detail screens reuse these fields read-only.
Routing to the manager from Active Directory, approve and reject dialogs, reason required on reject, edit and resubmit after rejection.

lines.item: Cancel by the employee before the leave starts
lines.note: Not an approval: one confirmation, allowed from Pending and from Approved, with a date check and an e-mail to the manager. Likely below the usual rate for this block.

lines.item: Lists: My Applications, Pending Approvals, all applications for HR
lines.note: Two lists are in the spec (6 columns and 2 filters each). The third is assumed: the HR Admin role 'views all applications' but has no screen for it yet.
4 stat cards: three status counts and the leave balance. The balance is a calculation, not a count.

lines.item: Active Directory sign-in and line manager lookup
lines.note: Sign-in plus the manager attribute for routing.
Approved, rejected and cancelled are in the requirements. A fourth, to the manager on submission, is assumed.

lines.item: Roles: Employee, Line Manager, HR Admin
lines.note: Each has its own menu and data scope (own, direct reports, all).
The retention NFR mentions an audit trail; which actions it records is not specified.
Development to test, test to production.

lines.item: Internal testing and fixes before UAT

risks.item: Working-day calculation needs a public holiday calendar, half days or state-specific weekends
risks.note: The requirement says 'working days' and nothing else. A maintained holiday calendar is one more master-data screen plus the calculation.

risks.item: Leave balance rules: entitlement per year, carry-forward, pro-rating, blocking applications above the balance
risks.note: The dashboard shows a balance but no requirement defines it.

risks.item: HR reporting grows into an export or a report
risks.note: HR Admin views all applications 'for reporting'; no export or report is specified.

risks.item: Manager absent or missing in Active Directory: delegation, escalation or reminders
risks.note: Nothing is specified for an application that nobody acts on.

assumptions: Counted from spec v0.1 of the sample project. The spec has no scope of work, so there is no comparison with sold mandays.
One approval level: the line manager only.
HR Admin gets one list of all applications with filters; no export, no report.
Four e-mail notifications: to the manager on submission and on cancellation, to the employee on approval and on rejection.
Number of Days counts Monday to Friday between the two dates, with no public holiday calendar and no half days.
The leave balance on the dashboard is entitlement minus approved days in the current year, with no carry-forward or pro-rating.
Two environment migrations: development to test, test to production.
Rates and shares come from the knowledge base. This sample carries none of its own, so a line is priced only where your knowledge base has a figure.
The open questions are listed but not sized: no lead developer has put mandays on them.
Not included: requirement workshops, UAT support, training, user documentation, data migration and warranty.

gap_patterns.why: Two calculations have no rule: Number of Days (working days) and the leave balance on the dashboard.
Cancel is specified, but not whether an approved application can be changed, or whether a cancellation needs approval.
HR Admin views all applications 'for reporting' with no screen, export or report defined.
Routing depends on one line manager from Active Directory; nothing covers absence or a missing manager.
The e-mail on submission is not stated, and the spec's notification list is empty.
The HR Admin role must come from somewhere: an AD group or in-app assignment is not stated.

questions.question: How is the leave balance worked out: entitlement per leave type per year minus approved days? Does unused leave carry forward, is it pro-rated for new joiners, and must the system stop an application that exceeds the balance?
Which days count as working days: are public holidays excluded, who keeps the holiday list up to date, and can someone take half a day?
What should happen when the line manager is on leave, has left, or the employee has no manager on record: can someone else approve, and should anyone be reminded?
What does HR need from all applications: a list to look things up, a file to download, or a monthly report? With which columns and for which period?
After an application is approved, can the employee change the dates or only cancel it? Does the manager need to approve a cancellation?
Which actions must the audit trail record, and who needs to see it?
Lead developer: what are the rates for the building blocks this project uses, and the shares for testing and project management?
